gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: It is Saturday tomorrow, so I ___ get up early.
gaps.hint: an absence of obligation at weekends
gaps.explanation: 'Don't have to' shows there is no obligation: don't have to get up.

gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ to leave the gallery by 6 p.m.
gaps.hint: have to takes the full infinitive
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' takes the full infinitive with 'to': have to leave.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have left the door unlocked — anyone could have walked in.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' blames someone for a past act: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: This bill ___ be right — we only ordered two coffees.
gaps.hint: an obvious mistake, so it is impossible
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' shows the speaker believes something is not possible: can't be right.

gaps.sentence: You ___ touch that wire — it carries a live current!
gaps.explanation: 'Mustn't' signals something absolutely not allowed: mustn't touch.

gaps.sentence: I am afraid you ___ park here without a resident's permit.
gaps.hint: permission that is refused with cannot

gaps.sentence: I ___ work late every Wednesday this month; it is a new company policy.
gaps.hint: obligation imposed by an external rule
gaps.explanation: 'Have to' expresses obligation imposed by external rules: have to work.
